supporting_observations.claim: The recurring HTTPS proxy connections in the evidence go to update.casebinder.com and occur at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:42, 13:47, 13:52, 13:57, 14:02, 14:07, and 14:11 UTC.
The CaseBinder updater process was running on WS-NKIM-01, and endpoint network events attribute its proxy connections to that executable.

The observed destination and cadence match the inventory's description of the approved CaseBinder updater checking update.casebinder.com about every five minutes, supporting a benign disposition for the alerted activity.
The updater process exited shortly after its last observed periodic connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnel metadata, not the contents of the encrypted HTTPS sessions.
The first listed CaseBinder-attributed connection is at 13:42 UTC; the supplied records do not attribute the earlier 13:30:34 UTC HTTPS connection to the CaseBinder updater.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish the contents or purpose of data exchanged inside the encrypted CaseBinder sessions.
The records do not establish the integrity or signature status of the CaseBinder updater executable.
The records do not establish whether the 13:30:34 UTC connection to docs.google.com is part of the alerted periodic activity.
unrelated_findings: At 13:30:34 UTC, WS-NKIM-01 made an HTTPS proxy connection to docs.google.com using a Chrome user agent. Google Docs is not listed as approved in the supplied inventory; review separately whether this use was authorized. This single connection is not evidence for the recurring CaseBinder activity. (T166-00051, T166-00052)

A Dropbox updater executable ran as SYSTEM on WS-NKIM-01. Dropbox is not listed as an approved service; review separately whether the installation or execution was authorized. These records alone do not establish Dropbox file-sharing or synchronization activity. (T166-00227, T166-00228, T166-00230, T166-00231)
